summary: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner (attested 2005). She held a post at the University of Manchester (attested 2005).

Jacques André (1910–1994) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. After studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1930–1948), he held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot (1877–1965) studied Tibetology and linguistics under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot in 1908. He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1919; director of studies from 1936) and the University of Paris (~1936–1958).

Jacques Gernet (1921–2018) studied classics and Chinese at Algiers, INALCO, and the EPHE. A sinologist and historian, he held posts at the EPHE, University of Paris, and Collège de France (1975–1992), and co-founded Paris Diderot University.

Jacques Giès (1950–2021) was a sinologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Flora Blanchon and at Paris-Sorbonne University. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and École du Louvre (1998–2008), and served as president of Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from INALCO, Paris-Sorbonne, and Luxembourg, completing his PhD under Denise Bernot. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and joined the EFEO in 2001.

Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate under Constantin Régamey (~1950–1957), served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and the EFEO (~1962–1981), and was a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1977–1992).

Jacques Scheuer (born 1942) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau (~1970–1976), and served as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1976–2007).

Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was a historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta (M.A. ~1892). His major posts included positions at Patna College (1899–1926), Banaras Hindu University (1917–1919), and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Jae-gwon Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2007 and subsequently held a post there.

Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indology scholar who held positions at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, where he was attested from 1924 to 1930 and served as Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji (born 1875) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge. He served as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911).

Jagannath Upadhyaya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at CIHTS in 1985.

Jagdish Kashyap (1908–1976), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and Vidyalankara Pirivena. He was a professor at Banaras Hindu University (~1940–1951) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh (1893–1986) worked in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Srikrishna Harihirlekar and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from CUNY Graduate Center. He held posts at Brown University (attested 2013–2018), CCNY, and New York University.

Jakob Steiner (1796–1863) studied at the University of Heidelberg (1818–1821) and the University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and the University of Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962), a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Oxford and under Richard von Garbe at Tübingen. He held posts at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and as chair at the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy Hugh Barrett, and UCLA under Robert Buswell. He held posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University (attested 2010–2017).

James A. Santucci is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He served as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).
